Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Nova Health

Hi Samantha / Rajiv -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone has a single source of truth. Let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you described:
- Latency spikes during daytime peaks causing degraded user experience for clinical staff (95th p95 moving from ~120ms to >600ms during bursts).
- Data isolation requirement for PHI workloads; Nova needs a private, VPC-isolated environment with customer-managed keys.
- Predictable monthly unit cost for budgeting - current variability on shared endpoints is hard to plan for.

Goals you shared:
- Dedicated GPU pool that can sustain 200 concurrent sessions with 8k context models for inference, targeting 99.5% uptime and p95 generation latency under 250ms for standard prompts.
- End-to-end SOC 2 evidence and single-tenant networking for compliance sign-off.
- Ability to scale capacity by predictable increments (add 4 GPUs per scale-up event) with a clear process for burst capacity.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated config (high-level):
- Baseline: 8x A100-style GPUs reserved (NVMe-backed local cache), isolated VPC deployment.
- Scaling: Autoscaler configured to add 4 GPUs on sustained queue growth > 5 minutes; manual burst option for +8 GPUs for 24/48h with pre-approved billing.
- SLA targets: 99.5% monthly uptime SLA, latency SLOs per-route with automated fallback to a compatible smaller model when load exceeds capacity.
- Security: Customer-managed KMS integration, audit logs shipped to your SIEM, SOC 2 attestation (see attached summary).

Attachments: I attached the initial Dedicated Proposal (NovaHealth_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a short SOC2 summary. These include the pricing bands, escalation contacts, and a draft mutual action plan.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marissa: share proposal + SOC2 summary (attached) - DONE (see above).
2) Samantha/Rajiv: confirm target SLA and any additional compliance questions by EOD Friday, 12/4.
3) Dev/Vivek: schedule a short technical deep-dive on infra and network requirements (30-45m) next week - suggested slots Wed/Thu morning PT.
4) Nova procurement: share any standard contract terms or procurement timeline; if you want, we can prepare a redline-friendly draft DOCUSIGN link.

If this aligns, I'll loop in our contracts lead and prepare a tailored term sheet for the Reserved Capacity commit.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. This looks good overall. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) SLA: 99.5% sounds reasonable but we need clarity on the measurement window and remedies (credits, support response SLA). Can you include the exact language you'd propose for the term sheet?
2) Scaling: our peak windows are typically 08:00-11:00 ET and 18:00-20:00 ET. The autoscale trigger you mentioned sounds fine, but can we have a provision for scheduled scale-ups aligned to known peak windows to avoid cold scaling latency?
3) Compliance: Priya (cc'd) owns procurement/compliance. Priya - we'll need the SOC 2 artifact and evidence of KMS integration.

We'll also want a network diagram (VPC peering options) and a short runbook for failover behavior if the Dedicated pool becomes saturated. Could Dev/ Vivek handle those?

I'll get back on procurement timeline by Friday.

Best,

Thanks Samantha - quick technical clarifications and a proposed initial sizing to validate against your traffic patterns.

Technical clarifications/proposal:
- Model profile: assume a 8k-context encoder-decoder model (roughly equivalent to an LLaMA 2-70B inference profile) with KV cache sized for 8k sequences.
- Baseline reserved: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (low-latency config), each serving ~25 concurrent sessions for the above model profile under sustained load (gives ~200 concurrent sessions aggregate).
- Burst policy: scheduled scale-ups (recommended) - we can pre-provision an extra 4 GPUs for known windows; autoscaler still preferred for unexpected spikes.
- Warmup/cache: we recommend a 10-15 minute scheduled warmup prior to heavy scheduled windows to pre-populate KV cache and avoid cold-start latency.
- Network: VPC peering + transit gateway works; we can provide a reference network diagram and a Terraform snippet for the peering.
- SLA measurement: rolling 30-day window for uptime; Support response targets: P1 within 30 minutes, P2 within 4 hours. Credit language: pro-rated credit for violations > 0.5% monthly. We'll include precise term language in the legal draft.

I'll attach the draft network diagram and a short runbook in the follow-up note (attaching SOC2 summary here as referenced). Happy to take 30-45m next week; I have Wed 11-12 PT or Thu 09-10 PT open.

-

Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
